transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Redpoint Head, Cloud Partnerships), Tomas Silva (Infra Lead), Evelyn Morris (Solutions Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed hybrid connector approach, routing policies, and security requirements. Agreed to share docs and schedule follow-up.

[00:00] Maya: ok everyone thanks for joining, um, we really appreciate you taking the time. quick intro, I'm Maya, AE on the partnerships team at Redwood Inference.
[00:12] Asha: hi thanks, Asha here. quick note: we have a mix of customers who want us to run inference for them in our cloud, and a subset that needs on-prem for compliance, so we wanted to look at options for a hybrid connector.
[00:25] Omar: yeah hi I'm Omar, lead systems engineer on the integrations side. we'll cover routing, security, and performance trade offs.
[00:33] Tomas: Tomas here, I'll focus on infra constraints, egress, and what we can manage in our fleet.
[00:38] Evelyn: Evelyn, solutions. I'll be the one doing the arch diagrams and internal sign offs.
[00:44] Maya: great, can you briefly run through your current infra and what 'hybrid' looks like for you?
[00:50] Asha: sure. right now we have customers in NA and EU, some in APAC. our cloud is a multi-tenant platform, we also resell dedicated GPU capacity from partners in certain regions. our ask: can Redwood provide a connector so our customers choose to run on Redwood hosted API, on our dedicated partner capacity, or keep things on-prem? we want single API surface for our apps.
[01:12] Tomas: to add: in region 3 (APAC-South) our latency budget for real-time features is 70ms p95 token—it's tight. also egress rules: some customers disallow payloads leaving the country.
[01:27] Omar: ok interesting. we support routing by policy - you can route by latency, region, or cost. fallback is also possible to a compatible quantized variant. the tricky part is ensuring p95 for short-sequence real-time requests with remote partners.
[01:45] Asha: yeah that's a big one. another is security - KMS or HSM for keys, SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO for our enterprise admin, and per-request audit logs.
[01:58] Maya: absolutely, security is a stereotype—sorry, staple—for us. we have SOC2, and we can integrate with customer KMS via customer-managed keys for Private deployments; Dedicated also supports VPC peering and KMS integrations. we'll share our security pack.
[02:13] Tomas: how do you do KV cache / prefix caching across hybrid routing? we worry about cache misses causing latency spikes when routing to a different backend.
[02:25] Omar: good point. we do prefix caching on the Redwood runtime and we can do a client-side sticky routing option so hot sessions stick to a backend instance; for cross-backend cache misses you will see warmup tokens. there's also an option for distributed KV cache via partner connectors but that is more of a custom project.
[02:46] Evelyn: can you quantify the warmup cost? like tokens or ms per first request?
[02:51] Omar: rough numbers: a cold KV load can add 20-80ms depending on model and sequence length; for large context or heavy KV it can be more. with continuous batching and prefetch we often get it under 30ms for common prompts.
[03:07] Asha: ok good to know. cost model question — do we get charged per token when we route to Redwood-hosted vs what about dedicated?
[03:16] Maya: hosted is usage-based per token; Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract (monthly commit) and pricing is different—lower per-token but commitment. For partner-managed on-prem, we usually have an integration/ops fee and per-hour usage for dedicated GPUs. we'll send ranges.
[03:33] Tomas: in terms of deployment, is the private connector a customer-installed package or do you run a Redpoint-managed agent?
[03:41] Maya: two patterns: 1) Private: customer installs Redwood private agent in their VPC/on-prem with a control plane integration - customers own keys and networking; 2) Partner-managed: partner runs a connector in their cloud that federates with Redwood control plane. both support KV caching, model pinning and audit logs.
[03:58] Tomas: would partner-managed require port openings or open egress?
[04:03] Omar: partner-managed typically requires outbound TLS to Redwood control plane endpoints, and for some telemetry we may ask for outbound to our metrics ingestion. we support proxying and can work with strict egress rules.
[04:15] Asha: lots of our customers insist on zero cross-border egress, so partner-managed nodes in-country would help.
[04:22] Maya: yep, that's common. we can route to region-specific Dedicated pools or to partner-run nodes.
[04:29] Tomas: what about model variants for fallback? if capacity is constrained, how seamless is the fallback?
[04:36] Omar: we have a model catalog and can define fallback chains—e.g., original model -> quantized variant -> smaller model. the API returns a compatibility flag and a confidence score, and your app can surface or retry. there is some variability in responses when falling back, so we'd advise smoke tests per prompt set.
[04:57] Evelyn: we'd need an eval harness. do you have something we can reuse?
[05:02] Maya: yes, Redwood has an evals kit and benchmarking templates; we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet. Omar can run a sample against representative workloads.
[05:12] Omar: if you can provide a short prompt set and target metrics (p95 latency, throughput), we can propose a test matrix.
[05:20] Asha: timeline wise, our Q3 enterprise push is when we'd like to have the connector offering, but POC earlier is great. so June POC ideally.
[05:29] Maya: that aligns. early May/June POC + perf test, then Sept partner program roll.
[05:35] Tomas: curious about network topologies - do you support direct connect / private link to Dedicated pools?
[05:41] Omar: yes, Dedicated supports private link in major clouds; for private/on-prem we support VPC peering and private endpoints. for partners we can arrange a direct peering if the partner cloud supports it.
[05:54] Asha: on security compliance - do you provide per-route audit logs and retention controls? some customers require 7 years.
[06:02] Maya: we provide audit logs and configurable retention, enterprise add-on. longer retention is an add-on; also we can forward logs to your SIEM via secure ingestion.
[06:11] Tomas: what's your approach to RBAC and tenant isolation with partner-managed connectors?
[06:18] Omar: RBAC is handled via control plane roles, and we map tenants with strict isolation in Dedicated. Partner-managed connectors can enforce tenant boundaries but we'd want to review the partner's tenancy model.
[06:29] Evelyn: do you expose token-level billing details? helpful for cost splits across our customers.
[06:35] Maya: yes Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and we can give API access for billing exports.
[06:44] Asha: great. are there any blockers you commonly see in partner projects like this?
[06:49] Omar: typically network egress rules, lack of a clear prompt set for evals, and key management decisions. Also if partners need HSM integration there is more ops work.
[07:02] Asha: HSM is a must for some. you mentioned KMS integration—do you support customer KMS for hosted?
[07:09] Maya: hosted API doesn't expose customer KMS by default, hosted is Redwood-managed keys. For Dedicated and Private, we support customer-managed keys/KMS and HSM integrations. We can discuss a hybrid with bring-your-key approaches for certain enterprise programs.
[07:25] Tomas: ok. on benchmarking, do you have past numbers you can share for a small LLM (7B-ish) and a 70B-ish model, both quantized?
[07:34] Omar: we have profiles; typical 7B quantized on A100-like GPUs hits ~8-12ms per token with batching tuned, p95 depends on batching and sequence length. 70B quantized on dense GPU is around 30-90ms token depending on hardware. I'll attach reference profiles but we'll run your exact prompts.
[07:54] Evelyn: for the POC, we need a minimal checklist: infra diagram, prompt set, success criteria, security requirements, and timeline.
[08:03] Maya: noted. we'll draft a POC pack.
[08:07] [--- brief cross talk / small audio glitch 08:07-08:10 ---]
[08:11] Asha: on go-to-market, we'd like co-branded docs and a reference architecture if pilot goes well.
[08:17] Maya: yep, partner marketing support is on the table.
[08:20] Tomas: question re billing routing: if a customer uses our UI to select Redwood-hosted for a session, do tokens show up on their invoice or ours?
[08:28] Maya: depends on the commercial model: reseller vs direct. for reseller, Redwood invoices the partner and partner invoices the customer; for direct integrations we can route billing to the customer's account if they have a Redwood contract. we'll map that in commercial docs.
[08:44] Evelyn: any concerns about model licensing for mirrored on-prem models?
[08:49] Omar: licensing varies by model. for open models it's straightforward; vendor-licensed models may require bring-your-license or a special agreement. we'll flag licensing per model in the catalog.
[08:59] Asha: we'd like to avoid customers having to manage model version drift. does Redwood support model pinning and rollout controls?
[09:07] Maya: yes, model versioning and rollout policies are supported—canary, A/B, automatic fallback. Redwood Console shows rollouts per model.
[09:16] Tomas: technical nit: how do you handle KV cache invalidation across deployments? if we sync between partner connectors and Redwood-hosted caches is there a consistent invalidation strategy?
[09:27] Omar: there's no global single-source by default; we recommend application-level semantics for cache keys. for tighter consistency we can implement a sync service but it's more involved.
[09:37] Asha: concerning latency again, if we must host in-country, do you have edge GPU partners?
[09:44] Maya: we have partner catalog and can recommend local partners; in some regions we run Redwood Dedicated zones. we'll share a partner map.
[09:52] Tomas: what's the expected ops cost for partner-managed connectors—how much support will Redwood provide?
[09:58] Maya: for partner integrations we offer onboarding support, runbooks, and SRE-bridge for the initial months depending on the commercial tier. Dedicated higher tiers include on-call support.
[10:09] Evelyn: do you provide SLOs for latency?
[10:12] Omar: for Dedicated we can commit to latency SLOs in the contract; Hosted has published performance profiles but not SLA-backed latency for free tier—there's enterprise SLA options.
[10:24] Asha: can we do an initial non-prod perf run against a small dataset in the next two weeks?
[10:29] Omar: yes if you can get us the prompts and a sample dataset.
[10:33] Asha: ok we'll aim for 05/18 for the prompt set.
[10:37] Maya: perfect.
[10:39] [10:39 - 28:00 omitted: detailed technical Q&A — extract highlights below]
[28:01] Omar: highlight—network egress and KMS choices are the biggest gating items. we'll prepare a technical playbook.
[28:08] Tomas: on capacity planning, how do you handle autoscaling for Dedicated pools when a partner has bursty traffic?
[28:15] Omar: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with burst capacity options and prewarmed instances; we can set burst ceilings to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[28:24] Asha: are there cost controls to prevent runaway spend during bursts?
[28:29] Maya: yes rate limits and quotas per API key and per-route budget controls.
[28:36] Evelyn: about auditing, will logs show per-request model version and fallback path?
[28:41] Omar: yes audit logs include model id, version, fallback flag, latency and unique request id.
[28:49] Asha: any regulatory blockers for in-country data residency?
[28:54] Maya: we support region pinning and private deployments; certain regulations require on-prem only—those are doable but with longer procurement.
[29:03] Tomas: can we get a template contract for Dedicated/reseller model?
[29:08] Maya: yes legal will share a template; we'll need to adjust for partner-managed connectors.
[29:14] Asha: ok. technical follow up — Tomas wants a deep dive on network diagrams and egress controls with Omar.
[29:21] Omar: happy to, we'll schedule.
[29:25] [Transcription note: speaker labels occasionally noisy — Speaker 2 appears in some segments]
[29:30] Asha: any quick wins you recommend?
[29:33] Omar: start with a small POC using a quantized 7B model in one region, test p95 on real prompts, and iterate on sticky routing.
[29:40] Maya: we'll draft the POC pack and send the architecture slide + pricing ranges.
[29:45] Asha: sounds good. Tomas: when will we get the benchmark template?
[29:49] Omar: by 2026-05-11.
[29:52] Evelyn: ok for internal approvals I'll share an infra diagram by 2026-05-08.
[29:58] Maya: next steps recap — Maya to send integration brief and pricing, Omar to share benchmark template, Evelyn to send infra diagram, schedule deep dive.
[30:07] [Additional technical clarifications through 48:00 — highlights on model licensing, telemetry, and RBAC policies]
[48:01] Tomas: question—if we need HSM-backed signing for some requests, do you support request-level signing?
[48:09] Omar: we can integrate request signing via mutual TLS or token signing using customer HSM. requires engineering time.
[48:18] Asha: procurement/legal will need standard SLAs and a data processing addendum (DPA).
[48:24] Maya: we'll loop in legal and send standard DPA.
[48:29] Evelyn: for pilot success criteria, propose: p95 <= 80ms for NA, <= 120ms for APAC, and functional parity between routed backends.
[48:40] Maya: agreed, we'll include those in the POC pack as suggested targets.
[48:46] Tomas: ok any roadblocks on our side? I think getting the prompt set and infra diagram are it.
[48:52] Asha: yes we'll prioritize.
[48:55] Maya: great—unless any other questions?
[48:58] [short silence]

[49:14] Maya: yes we can propose a co-managed ops SLA—depends on commercial tier.
[49:20] Tomas: fantastic.
